question: Why does the devotee take refuge in Kālī despite her transcendence of the Vedas?
premises: Kālī is not within the range of the Vedas.
She is praised by the wise.
The speaker takes refuge in her.
inference: Though beyond Vedic grasp, Kālī is worthy of refuge and praised by the wise.
plain_english: She is indeed not within the range of the Vedas in any way, yet praised by the wise; I take refuge in her.
